The model was 1.15 times the actual scale of the NASA LeRC High-Temperature, Cooled, Radial Turbine.
Twelve orifices were used in the discharge flow-control plate at the model exit to regulate the distribution of trailing edge flow.
The inner passage exit orifice diameter was twice that of the middle and outer exit passages.
The model was oriented 32.7 degrees from the plane of the test section to match the full-scale rotor.
Chromel-Alumel, thin-film surface thermocouples (13 microns thick) were used to measure local wall temperatures.
Liquid crystal temperature indicating paints were used in addition to the thermocouples.
The maximum shaft speed for the experiments was 750 RPM, producing body forces up to 10,000 g's at the model root.
Transient heat transfer tests were conducted at Reynolds numbers of 1/4, 1/2, and equal to the full-scale turbine.
Rotation generally increased heat transfer on some sides of the radial passages and decreased it on others.
Heat transfer in the tri-passage axial flow region was relatively unaffected by rotation.
In the transitional region, heat transfer on one surface decreased to 20% of the stationary values with rotation.
Comparisons to previous 3D numerical studies showed both agreement and disagreement with the experimental results.
The thermocouple data was smoothed using a second-order least squares fit to remove random noise.
The maximum air flowrate to the model was approximately 0.02 kg/s (0.044 lbm/s).
The model air was cooled to -12°C (10°F) before entering the rotating shaft and heated to 10°C (50°F) at the model inlet.
